coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Bridgeview paseo, Mission Rock
record.summary: Pedestrian paseo on Bridgeview Street north of Exposition Street (the street name used in the 2018 Design Controls), next to Block G (the Visa building) and Block K on Pier & Point's mapped geometry. The 2019 Phase 1 submittal planned it as part of Phase 1, and in February 2025 Port staff listed 'the paseos in the bottom around Building G leading in to China Basin Park' among the Phase 1 public improvements put to the Commission for acceptance as Port owned; a June 2026 Port staff report says 'the City has accepted all public infrastructure, including parks, streets, and public utilities within the Phase', without naming this paseo.

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock Design Controls (their April 24, 2018 final version names this planned street Bridgeview Street (Section 4.4, p.98; the earlier version the Commission approved was not read)); the Port's Jan 26, 2018 staff report requested this approval under Resolution 18-04, and its Sept 2019 memo dates the Commission's approvals January 30, 2018 (it numbers the Design Controls resolution 18-05)

changes.text: The record is renamed from 'Bridgeview Street paseo' to 'Bridgeview paseo, Mission Rock', so it is not confused with the walkway between Mission Bay Blocks 9 and 9A (record 8719004), which is another segment of the Bridgeview Way alignment. The old names still find the record in search and the old page address redirects. Status, shape and use are unchanged.

changes.text: On the Bridgeview Street paseo (Bridgeview Way, north segment) timeline, the February 11, 2025 infrastructure acceptance used to appear twice, from two tables with different wording; it now appears once. The entry that stays now sets the status to complete, cites the Port's June 2026 memo and says the minutes do not name this paseo. Dates and statuses are unchanged and no source was dropped.

In February 2025 Port staff listed the paseos around Building G among the Phase 1 improvements put to the Port Commission for acceptance; a June 2026 Port staff report (dated June 5) says the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure without naming this paseo. No Port document read says what Exposition Street is called now.

The January 30, 2018 Design Controls approval milestone now says the street or open-space name comes from the April 24, 2018 final version of the Design Controls, and cites the Port's January 2018 and September 2019 memos for the approval. Those memos give different resolution numbers (18-04 and 18-05).
Added a record for the Bridgeview Street paseo.

The status stays complete, but the record's notes and its earlier change entry no longer say the paseo was built on the strength of the 2019 Phase 1 submittal, which was only a forecast. They now cite the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes (staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure, including the paseos around Building G) and the Port's June 2026 report (Phase 1 completed in 2025; the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure); neither names this paseo individually. The Jan 30, 2018 Design Controls approval milestone now cites the Sept 2019 Port memo that states the date, and notes that the memo numbers that resolution 18-05 while the January 26 staff report requested it as 18-04.

changes.text: The Feb 11, 2025 milestone said the Port Commission accepted Mission Rock Phase 1's streets and paseos 'including this one'. The minutes record Resolution 25-05 authorizing Port staff to accept the public infrastructure the developer built (streets, sidewalks, parks and open spaces), with Board of Supervisors action still to follow, and do not name this paseo individually. The milestone now says so, and cites the Port's June 2026 memo, which says the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure.

The Bridgeview Street paseo between the Visa building and Block K added on its real lot. The 2019 Phase 1 submittal planned it as part of Phase 1; the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes record staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure, including the paseos around Building G (Resolutions 25-05, 25-06), and the Port's June 2026 report says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure.

open_questions: No source read names this paseo on its own as built or accepted. The 'complete' status rests on the Port's general statements that Phase 1 public infrastructure, including the paseos around Building G, was accepted (Feb 2025 minutes, June 2026 report); the site was not checked against imagery or a site visit.
Acceptance date and construction cost for this paseo are not published separately in any source read.

No Port document read says what Exposition Street is called now. The Port's 2020 street-names staff report proposed 'Spur Street' to replace 'Exposition Street', and the Port's October 2023 report lists 'Approval of new street names honoring Dr. Maya Angelou and Toni Stone', without saying which street took which name.

record.notes: Bridgeview paseo, Mission Rock, 1044 Bridgeview Way -- the pedestrian paseo between Block G/Visa and Block K, from Exposition Street (Toni Stone Crossing) to China Basin Park; Design Controls Figure 3.1.1 marks it as Paseo 4.4. Built with Phase 1, per Port records of its acceptance: the 2019 Phase 1 submittal only planned it (Phase 1 'will also complete the Shared Public Way and Bridgeview Street paseos north of Exposition Street'), but the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes record staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure and describe 'the paseos in the bottom around Building G leading in to China Basin Park' as Port owned (Resolutions 25-05, 25-06), and the Port's June 5, 2026 report says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and 'The City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure'. None of these names this paseo on its own. Its own real Assessor lot, 8719A007 (840 m2, addressed 1044 Bridgeview Way, recorded 2020-06-12); DataSF centerline CNN 15284000 (Bridgeview Way, END: NORTH to Toni Stone Xing, layer PRIVATE). Its east lot line is Block K's west edge. Added 2026-09-17.
